mainTopic: Practical life advice and lists of three: from רב, the people of ירושלים, and רבי יוחנן
overview: This amud first finishes an earlier discussion about שדים, explaining that they are found on the paths near a city. The גמרא then collects practical life advice from רב. He tells רב אסי where to live and about marriage. He tells רב כהנא to keep his word and do honest work, and he warns his son חייא against dangerous habits. A ברייתא adds three small beings one should not provoke, because they will grow strong. רב then teaches his son איבו business sense, which leads to a short discussion about selling dates to brewers, and רב פפא adds a warning against relying on credit. Next come two lists of three tips from the people of ירושלים, quoted by רבי יוחנן and רבי יהושע בן לוי. The amud ends with רבי יוחנן's lists of three who inherit עולם הבא and three whom הקדוש ברוך הוא praises every day. The story of רב ספרא that begins at the end continues on the next amud.

steps.title: שדים are found on the paths near the city
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes an earlier point: שדים are found on the paths near town, because their horses run off there and the שדים come to bring them back.
steps.simpleTranslation: They are found on the paths, because the horses run away and they come to lead them back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an answer from the previous section about where שדים are found. It says they are on the paths outside the city, not inside where people live.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question about how שדים could be near a settled place came on the previous amud. The answer limits the danger to the paths at the edge of town. The reason given is that the שדים' horses wander there and the שדים come to lead them back. In general, שדים do not enter places where people live.

keyTerms.meaning: Paths or roads at the edges of a town
They slip away or run off

steps.confusionAlert: This line is the end of a discussion that started earlier. Do not read it as a new topic. It answers a question that was already asked.

phrases.english: They are on the paths,
phrases.notes: The subject is the שדים from the earlier discussion.

phrases.english: because the horses run away,
phrases.notes: These are the שדים' own horses.

phrases.english: and they come to lead them back.
phrases.notes: So the שדים end up on the paths near town.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a discussion about שדים earlier.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Where exactly near a city are שדים found? (asked earlier)
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: On the outlying paths, where their horses wander and they come to retrieve them.

steps.title: רב's advice to רב אסי about where to live and about marriage
steps.stepSummary: רב tells רב אסי not to live in a city without horses and dogs, not to live in a city whose leader is a doctor, and not to marry two wives. If he does marry two, he should marry a third.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב said to רב אסי: Do not live in a city where no horse neighs and no dog barks. And do not live in a city whose head is a doctor. And do not marry two wives. If you married two, marry three.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new collection of practical advice from רב. Here he speaks to his student רב אסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Horses and dogs make noise that warns of intruders, so a town without them is less safe. A doctor who leads a town will be too busy with his patients to govern well. Two wives may join together against their husband, but a third wife would tell him about their plans.

keyTerms.meaning: The head or leader of the city

phrases.english: And Rav said to Rav Asi:
Do not live in a city
where no horse neighs
phrases.notes: Animals give warning and protection.

phrases.english: and no dog barks.
And do not live in a city
whose head is a doctor,
phrases.notes: He will be too busy to govern well.

phrases.english: and do not marry two wives.
phrases.notes: They may plot together against you.

phrases.english: If you married two,
marry three.
phrases.notes: The third will tell you about the other two's plans.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new collection of רב's advice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Live in a protected, well-run city, and avoid marrying exactly two wives.

steps.title: Keep your word and do honest work even if it is lowly
steps.stepSummary: רב tells רב כהנא that it is better to do dirty work than to break your word. He should even skin a carcass in the market for pay, and not say the work is beneath him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said to רב כהנא: Turn over a carcass, but do not turn over your words. Skin a carcass in the market and take wages, and do not say, 'I am a כהן, I am a great man, and this work disgusts me.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב now gives advice to his student רב כהנא about honesty and about not being too proud to earn a living.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first line plays on the word 'turn over'. Turning over a dead animal is unpleasant, but it is better than turning back on a promise. The second line teaches that even the dirtiest paid work is better than refusing work out of pride and then depending on others. Being a כהן or an important person is no excuse.

keyTerms.meaning: A carcass, an animal that died without proper slaughter
This thing is hateful or disgusting to me

steps.whyThisMatters: This is one of the best-known lines in חז"ל about the dignity of work and the duty to support yourself rather than rely on others.

phrases.english: Rav said to Rav Kahana:
Turn over a carcass,
but do not turn over your words.
phrases.notes: Do not go back on what you said.

phrases.english: Skin a carcass in the marketplace
and take wages,
and do not say, "I am a priest,
and I am a great man,
and this thing disgusts me."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the collection of רב's advice, now to a different student.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Keep your word, and do any honest work rather than depend on others out of pride.

steps.title: Carry food with you, and keep food carefully even when it is cheap
steps.stepSummary: רב tells רב כהנא to take food along even on a short trip, like going up to the roof. Even when food is very cheap, he should keep it close and treat it with care.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you go up to the roof, take your food with you. Even if a hundred pumpkins cost a זוז in the city, keep them under the corners of your garment.
steps.whatsHappening: רב continues his advice to רב כהנא with two short sayings about food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Going up to the roof is a very short trip, but you should still bring food, because you never know what will happen. A hundred pumpkins for a זוז means food is extremely cheap. Even so, you should keep your own supply close and handle it with respect. Some מפרשים read this as: make sure you have food of your own and do not rely on low prices lasting.

phrases.english: If you go up to the roof,
take your food with you.
phrases.notes: Even a short trip calls for food.

phrases.english: Even if a hundred pumpkins in the city cost a zuz,
let them be under the corners of your garment.
phrases.notes: Keep food close and treat it with care, even when it is cheap.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: More advice from רב to רב כהנא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Always have food with you, and value food even when it is cheap.

steps.title: רב warns his son חייא against five dangerous habits
steps.stepSummary: רב tells his son חייא not to drink medicines, not to jump over ditches, not to pull out a tooth, not to provoke a snake, and not to provoke a non-Jew.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said to his son חייא: Do not drink medicines, do not jump over a ditch, do not pull out a tooth, do not provoke a snake, and do not provoke a non-Jew.
steps.whatsHappening: רב now gives his son חייא five short warnings, each one about avoiding harm or danger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Drinking medicine regularly can make you dependent on it. Jumping a ditch can cause an injury. A bad tooth should be treated if possible rather than pulled. Provoking a snake, or a non-Jew who may take revenge, puts you in danger.
steps.whatToRemember: רב's advice to his students and his son is about practical wisdom: stay safe, keep your word, earn an honest living, and take care of your health and your food.

phrases.english: Rav said to Chiyya his son:
Do not drink medicines,
phrases.notes: You may come to depend on them.

phrases.english: and do not jump over a ditch,
and do not pull out a tooth,
phrases.notes: Try to heal it instead.

phrases.english: and do not provoke a snake,
and do not provoke a non-Jew.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רב's advice, now to his son.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Avoid habits and actions that risk your health or invite danger.

steps.title: Three small beings you should not provoke
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists three beings you should not pick fights with: a small גוי, a small snake, and a small תלמיד.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: There are three you should not provoke. These are a young non-Jew, a young snake, and a young student.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that fits the earlier advice from רב to his son חייא not to provoke a snake or a non-Jew. It adds a third item, a young תלמיד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 already warned against provoking a snake and a גוי. This ברייתא sharpens that advice: even when they are small and seem harmless, don't provoke them. It also adds a young Torah student to the list.

keyTerms.meaning: provoke, pick a fight with, stir up

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
Three — one should not provoke them,
and these are they:
a small non-Jew, and a small snake,
and a small (young) Torah student.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: שְׁלֹשָׁה אֵין מִתְקַנְּאִין בָּהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands step 5's warning about provoking a snake and a גוי into a three-item list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Do not provoke a young גוי, a young snake, or a young תלמיד.

steps.title: Why not: their power is waiting behind their ears
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason and answers that their future power stands "behind their ears." They will grow up and take revenge.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? Because their kingship stands behind their ears.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why these three are dangerous even when small. It answers that their power is right behind them, waiting to come.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is timing. Right now they look weak, but each one will grow up and become strong in its own way. The young גוי may come to political power, the snake will grow its venom, and the student will become a great scholar. Then each may avenge the person who hurt it.

keyTerms.meaning: behind their ears — meaning very close, about to arrive

phrases.english: What is the reason?
Because their kingship (power) stands behind their ears.
phrases.notes: Their future power is just behind them; they will grow up and get even.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason behind the ברייתא in step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why should one not provoke these three when they are small?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Their power is right behind them; they will grow up and take revenge.
steps.whatToRemember: Don't judge someone's danger by how small they are now. Small things grow.

steps.title: רב teaches איבו worldly wisdom: sell quickly, and sell wine without regret
steps.stepSummary: רב tells his son איבו that Torah study didn't succeed with him, so he will teach him practical matters. Sell your goods as soon as you arrive. Selling may bring regret, except selling wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said to his son איבו: I worked hard to teach you Torah, but it didn't succeed. Come, I will teach you worldly matters. While the dust is still on your feet, sell your merchandise. Anything you sell, you might regret, except wine, which you sell without regret.
steps.whatsHappening: A new set of advice begins, this time from רב to his son איבו. It is about business, not Torah study.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Tip one: sell right away when you come back from a trip, before prices drop. Tip two: with most goods, you might regret selling if prices later rise. Wine is different, because it can go sour and be lost completely, so selling it is always a good move.

keyTerms.meaning: while the dust is still on your feet

steps.confusionAlert: Here רב is speaking to איבו, a different son from חייא in step 5. Don't mix up the two sons.

phrases.english: Rav said to Ayvu, his son:
I toiled with you in Torah learning,
but the matter did not succeed.
Come, I will teach you worldly matters.
While the dust is still on your feet, sell your merchandise.
phrases.notes: Sell as soon as you return, before prices fall.

phrases.english: Anything — you may sell it and regret it,
except wine, which you sell and do not regret.
phrases.notes: Wine can spoil, so selling it is always wise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new set of רב's advice, now practical business tips to איבו.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sell your goods immediately on arrival, and never hesitate to sell wine.

steps.title: Take the money first, and choose a small safe profit
steps.stepSummary: רב continues: open your purse to get paid before you open your sack to deliver. A small gain close to home beats a big gain from far away.
steps.simpleTranslation: Untie your purse, then open your sack. Better a קב from the ground than a כור from the roof.
steps.whatsHappening: רב keeps giving איבו business tips. Here he gives two more.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First: get paid before you hand over the goods, so you won't be cheated. Second: a כור is much larger than a קב. Even so, a small, safe, nearby profit ("from the ground") is better than a big, risky one that is far off and hard to reach ("from the roof").

keyTerms.meaning: a כור — a very large measure

phrases.english: Untie your purse, then open your sack.
phrases.notes: Receive payment first, then deliver the goods.

phrases.english: A kav from the ground
and not a kor from the roof.
phrases.notes: A small, safe profit is better than a large, risky one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רב's business advice to איבו.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Collect payment before delivering, and prefer safe small gains over risky large ones.

steps.title: Have dates? Run and sell them to the brewer
steps.stepSummary: רב advises that if you have dates in storage, you should hurry to sell them to the beer-maker before they spoil.
steps.simpleTranslation: If there are dates in your storeroom, run to the brewery.
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives one more business tip to איבו, about dates. This tip leads into the next few lines of the גמרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Dates go bad if kept too long. The brewer uses dates to make beer, so he is a ready buyer. The logic is the same as with wine: sell spoilable goods quickly.

phrases.english: If there are dates in your storeroom,
run to the brewery (to sell them).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Last item in רב's advice to איבו; it sets up the follow-up discussion about dates and brewing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sell your dates quickly to the brewer before they spoil.

steps.title: How many dates may you keep? Up to three סאה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how much of the dates one may keep for himself. רבא answers: up to three סאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And up to how much? רבא said: up to three סאה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up question about רב's date advice, and רבא gives a measurement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב said to run and sell the dates. That raises a question: does this mean all of them? רבא sets a limit: you may keep up to three סאה for yourself and sell the rest.

phrases.english: And up to how much?
Rava said: Up to three se'ah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies how far step 10's advice reaches.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How many dates may one keep instead of selling?

steps.title: Brewing beer made me rich
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says he would not have become wealthy if not for brewing beer. Others say רב חסדא said it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: If I had not brewed beer, I would not have become rich. Some say רב חסדא said: If I had not brewed beer, I would not have become rich.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a personal statement that backs up the idea that the beer business is profitable. It also reports a disagreement about who said it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This supports the link between dates and the brewery: brewing is a real way to get rich. The words are exactly the same in both versions. The only question is whether רב פפא or רב חסדא said them.

keyTerms.meaning: some say — introduces a second version

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:

phrases.aramaic: אִי לָא דִּרְמַאי שִׁכְרָא לָא אִיעַתַּרִי.
phrases.english: If I had not brewed beer, I would not have become rich.
Some say: Rav Chisda said:

phrases.aramaic: אִי לָא דִּרְמַאי שִׁכְרָא לָא אִיעַתַּרִי:
phrases.english: If I had not brewed beer, I would not have become rich.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי לָא דִּרְמַאי שִׁכְרָא לָא אִיעַתַּרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the brewery theme of step 10 with personal testimony.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The beer business brought wealth (רב פפא, or in another version רב חסדא).
steps.confusionAlert: The two versions do not disagree about the content. They only disagree about who said it.

steps.title: סודנא means a pleasant secret and kindness
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the word סודנא (brewer) means. רב חסדא reads it as סוד נאה, a pleasant secret, and גמילות חסדים, acts of kindness.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is סודנא? רב חסדא said: a pleasant secret, and acts of kindness.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the word סודנא from רב's advice by breaking it into smaller word parts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא reads סודנא as סוד נאה, "a pleasant secret," because brewing is a quiet, good way to make money. He then adds גמילות חסדים, because the brewer's earnings also let him do kindness for others. So the trade is both profitable and a chance to do good.

phrases.english: What is "sudana"?
Rav Chisda said:
A pleasant secret, and acts of loving kindness.
phrases.notes: A wordplay on the letters of סודנא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the key word סודנא from step 10, closing the brewery discussion.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does the word סודנא mean?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: סוד נאה and גמילות חסדים — a fine, quiet livelihood that also lets one do kindness.
steps.whatToRemember: רב's advice to איבו is all about sensible, safe business: sell quickly, get paid first, and avoid risk. The brewery is praised as a good business that also allows חסד.

steps.title: Do not rely on credit or paper promises
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא warns that even money you have a legal claim to still has to be chased down. Selling on credit is risky, and even when the money comes, it comes badly.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Anything you own only through a document still has to be collected. Any sale on credit might get paid or might not. And even when it does get paid, it is 'bad money', meaning it comes late and in small, annoying pieces.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another piece of business advice, this time from רב פפא, about the risk of selling on credit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This continues the theme of step 9 ("open your purse before your sack"): cash in hand is better than a promise. רב פפא lists three levels of risk. A document gives you ownership, but you still have to collect. A credit sale may never be paid. Even when it is paid, the money is hard to collect and comes late.

keyTerms.meaning: Something held by means of a document or transfer, a legal claim rather than cash in hand
Collection, the work of actually getting the money
Credit, a sale where payment comes later
'Bad money': money that is slow and difficult to collect

steps.whyThisMatters: It completes רב's earlier advice ('open your purse before your sack') with a practical warning against relying on credit.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
Anything held by means of a document still requires collection.
phrases.notes: Even if you legally own it, you still have to go and get it.

phrases.english: Any sale on credit —
maybe the payment will come, maybe it will not come.
And even when it comes, it is bad money.
phrases.notes: It comes late and in bits.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of business advice
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Avoid relying on credit; cash in hand is safer.

steps.title: Three pieces of advice from the people of ירושלים, quoted by רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן quotes the people of ירושלים: in war, go out last so you can retreat first. Live simply on שבת rather than depend on others. Join up with someone who is having success.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said three things in the name of the people of ירושלים. (1) When you go out to war, do not go out at the front. Go out at the back, so that if there is a retreat you will be first back into the city. (2) Treat your שבת like a weekday, with simple meals, rather than needing help from other people. (3) Try to join up with someone whose luck is going well right now.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new set of three practical tips. רבי יוחנן quotes them from the people of ירושלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All three tips are about practical caution. Protect your life in war, protect your independence with money, and attach yourself to people who are succeeding. The second tip is striking: even honoring שבת with fancy food comes second to not depending on others.

keyTerms.meaning: The people of ירושלים, known for their wisdom
Make your שבת like a weekday (eat simply)
'The hour smiles at him': he is currently successful

steps.confusionAlert: 'Make your שבת like a weekday' does not mean breaking שבת. It only means eating simple weekday-style meals instead of borrowing money for fancy ones.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said three things
in the name of the people of Jerusalem:
When you go out to war —
do not go out first,
rather, go out last,
so that you will come back in first.
phrases.notes: If the army has to retreat, you reach the safety of the city first.

phrases.english: And make your Shabbat like a weekday,
and do not become dependent on other people.
And make an effort to join with someone
whom the hour is smiling upon.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלֹשָׁה דְּבָרִים אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם אַנְשֵׁי יְרוּשָׁלַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from business tips to a new set of general life advice
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Be cautious in war, stay financially independent, and join with successful people.

steps.title: Three pieces of advice from the people of ירושלים, quoted by רבי יהושע בן לוי
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי quotes three more tips: avoid shameful behavior because of what happened with דוד, marry off a grown daughter quickly even to a freed slave, and watch your wife's closeness to her first son-in-law.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said three things in the name of the people of ירושלים. (1) Do not get involved in shameful behavior, because of the well-known incident (דוד and בת שבע). (2) If your daughter has grown up, free your slave and marry her to him, rather than leave her unmarried. (3) Be careful about your wife and her first son-in-law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a parallel set of three tips. This time רבי יהושע בן לוי quotes them from the people of ירושלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These tips deal with family life and personal holiness. The third tip is left unexplained here, so it sets up the next step, where the גמרא asks what the danger actually is.

keyTerms.meaning: Shameful behavior. Some explain it as 'gardens', meaning secluded places
'The incident that happened': דוד and בת שבע
She has fully grown up (a בוגרת)

phrases.aramaic: שְׁלֹשָׁה דְּבָרִים אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said three things
in the name of the people of Jerusalem:
Do not indulge in shameful behavior,
because of the incident that happened.
phrases.notes: This is the story of דוד and בת שבע, told in שמואל ב chapter יא.

phrases.english: If your daughter has grown up —
free your slave and give him to her as a husband.
And be careful with your wife
regarding her first son-in-law.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלֹשָׁה דְּבָרִים אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי מִשּׁוּם אַנְשֵׁי יְרוּשָׁלַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel list of three tips from the same source, the people of ירושלים
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Avoid shameful behavior, marry off a grown daughter, and guard against a wife's closeness to her first son-in-law.

steps.title: Why be careful about the first son-in-law
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the danger with the first son-in-law is. רב חסדא says it is forbidden closeness. רב כהנא says it is money: she may give him your wealth.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? רב חסדא said: because of the risk of forbidden relations (ערוה). רב כהנא said: because of money, since she may pour your money onto him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the third tip, and two אמוראים give different explanations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The tip in step 16 did not say what the danger was. רב חסדא sees a moral danger, because the mother-in-law is very fond of her first son-in-law. רב כהנא sees a financial danger, because she might give him your money.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
Rav Chisda said: because of forbidden relations,
Rav Kahana said: because of money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the third tip of step 16
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What danger the warning about the first son-in-law refers to
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב חסדא: forbidden relations. רב כהנא: loss of money.

steps.title: Both dangers are real
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that both reasons are true, so one should be careful for both.
steps.simpleTranslation: This and that both exist: both dangers really happen.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the disagreement by saying both explanations are correct.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not a real argument where one side wins. The two reasons do not contradict each other, and both risks happen in real life. So the warning covers both.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This and that both exist': both are true

steps.whatToRemember: The warning about the first son-in-law covers both a moral danger and a financial danger.

phrases.english: This and that both exist.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the two explanations by accepting both
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both reasons apply; be careful on both counts.

steps.title: Three people who inherit עולם הבא
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן lists three kinds of people who inherit עולם הבא: one who lives in ארץ ישראל, one who raises his sons to learn תורה, and one who makes הבדלה over wine on מוצאי שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Three people are among those who inherit עולם הבא. They are: one who lives in ארץ ישראל, one who raises his sons to learn תורה, and one who makes הבדלה over wine on מוצאי שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves from practical advice to a list of three things that earn עולם הבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first two items are clearly big things. The third, making הבדלה over wine, seems small. That is why the גמרא will ask about it in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: One who makes הבדלה over wine

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
Three are among those who inherit the World to Come.
They are: one who lives in the Land of Israel,
and one who raises his sons to Torah study,
and one who makes havdala over wine
at the end of Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: שְׁלֹשָׁה מִנּוֹחֲלֵי הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new list, this time about rewards in עולם הבא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Living in ארץ ישראל, raising sons to learn תורה, and making הבדלה over wine earn עולם הבא.

steps.title: Saving wine from קידוש for הבדלה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what is so special about making הבדלה over wine. It answers: this is someone who has little wine and still saves some from קידוש for הבדלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is it? It is someone who saves some wine from קידוש so he will have wine for הבדלה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the third item is so great, and answers by describing exactly who is meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Simply making הבדלה over wine does not seem worth עולם הבא. The answer narrows the case: a person with very little wine who holds some back from קידוש so he can do הבדלה properly. That self-control and care for the מצוה is what earns the reward.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it? (What does this refer to?)

steps.whatToRemember: The reward is not for simply making הבדלה over wine. It is for the poor person who saves some of his קידוש wine so he can make הבדלה.

phrases.english: What is this?
One who leaves over wine from Kiddush for Havdala.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the third item in רבי יוחנן's list
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why making הבדלה over wine deserves עולם הבא
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It refers to someone with little wine who saves some from קידוש for הבדלה.

steps.title: Three people ה׳ praises every day
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says הקדוש ברוך הוא praises three people daily: a single man in a big city who does not sin, a poor person who returns a lost object, and a rich person who gives his tithes quietly.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: There are three people whom הקדוש ברוך הוא praises out loud every day. The first is a single man who lives in a big city and does not sin. The second is a poor person who returns a lost item to its owner. The third is a rich person who separates מעשר from his produce privately.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a new list of three special kinds of people. The list is a continuation of the earlier lists of three in this section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each person does the right thing exactly where it is hardest. A single man in a big city faces many temptations. A poor man badly needs the money he found. A rich man could easily show off his giving. ה׳ announces their praise because their goodness is rare and tested.

keyTerms.meaning: A large walled city, full of people and temptations

steps.whyThisMatters: This teaching shows a key idea: a good deed is worth more when it is done against a strong pull to do wrong, or without any wish for honor.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
Three people, He announces about them
The Holy One, Blessed be He, every day:
About a bachelor who lives in a big city
and does not sin,
phrases.notes: Meaning he does not sin with women, even though temptation is all around him.

phrases.english: and about a poor man who returns a lost object to its owner,
and about a rich man who tithes his produce privately.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, שְׁלֹשָׁה מַכְרִיז עֲלֵיהֶן הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בְּכׇל יוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new list of three from the same speaker, רבי יוחנן. It follows his earlier list of three who inherit עולם הבא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הקדוש ברוך הוא praises every day a single man in a city who does not sin, a poor man who returns a lost object, and a rich man who tithes privately.

steps.title: רב ספרא was a bachelor living in a city
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a story by noting that רב ספרא fit the first type in the list: a single man living in a big city.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ספרא was an unmarried man who lived in a big city.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a story about רב ספרא. It tells us he matched the first description in רבי יוחנן's list, and the story continues on the next amud (113b).
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line only gives background and does not finish the story yet. It links the teaching to a real person. This prepares us to see how רב ספרא reacted when he heard this praise.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא (Talmudic sage) who was unmarried and lived in a city

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new rule or teaching. It is only the opening of a story. Its point will become clear on the next amud.

phrases.aramaic: רַב סָפְרָא רַוּוֹק הַדָּר בִּכְרַךְ הֲוָה,
phrases.english: Rav Safra was a bachelor living in a big city,

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב סָפְרָא רַוּוֹק הַדָּר בִּכְרַךְ הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Introduces a real-life example of the first category in רבי יוחנן's list, as background for a story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Background fact: רב ספרא was a bachelor living in a city, and so he matched the first type in the list.
